findings.title: Unsubscribe changes state on a plain GET and toggles on every visit
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is reached by a GET (config/routes.rb lines 440-441) and runs `tu.save!` on every request, with no confirmation and no CSRF protection. Anything that fetches the URL changes the user's subscription: email link scanners and prefetchers, browser preloading, or a third-party page embedding `` for a logged-in user. The logic also toggles. If the level is above regular it drops to regular; otherwise it drops to muted. So a watching user who clicks once and later reloads the page (or reopens it from history) ends up muted, not just unsubscribed. Fix: make the GET page side-effect free (it already shows a notification dropdown) and do the change via POST/PUT, or use a signed token. At minimum, make the change idempotent rather than a toggle.

findings.title: NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body:
`TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users record for this topic. That happens, for example, when the user was emailed because they watch the category or because of a mention, and never visited the topic.

The next line calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, so the unsubscribe link produces a 500 error. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row when it is missing, or handle the nil case.

findings.title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change: no MessageBus publish or reason tracking
unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking other callers
findings.body:
The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` passes that value.

Any other email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` and no `unsubscribe_url` will fail. `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, which raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` (or renders a literal placeholder link) for those emails. The test spec had to be changed to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which hints at this.

Fix: use a separate key for the per-topic sentence and append it only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

findings.title: Message claims notifications stop although the level may only drop to regular
findings.body:
When the user was tracking or watching, the server only lowers the level to regular. At regular they still receive notifications for replies to them and mentions.

The page nevertheless says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>", which is misleading to users.
